title: Rollout pulse pocket and regional coverage cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick reference for a 72-hour rollout lane focused on regional coverage and minimal operator overhead. Not a full runbook — this is the pocket version for shift leads and coverage planners. Keep short, attach to the full runbook for run-of-release details.

High-level objectives:
- Release feature X with staged regional ramp over 72h.
- Maintain 99.9% latency SLO for host tier; <1% error rate regression.
- Validate telemetry gating (p95 latency, tail qps per shard, error budget burn).
- Contain blast radius via regional throttles and model-variant fallback.

Rollout windows (UTC):
- Phase A (canary): 2028-06-14 04:00 - 04:04 (4 min warmup) — region: us-west-2 (10k users/day cohort)
- Phase B (cohort expansion): 2028-06-14 05:00 - 06:00 — add eu-west-1 (gradual 5% -> 25%)
- Phase C (regional ramp): 2028-06-14 12:00 - 2028-06-16 12:00 — global progressive ramp to 100% with hold points

Staffing & coverage (pocket mapping):
- Primary owner: Jordan Reeves (release steward) — reachable on slack @jre (pager R1)
- On-call SRE: Asha Patel — first-line for infra/latency anomalies (pager S1)
- Serving runtime lead: Miguel Santos — model routing/fallback hooks (pager M1)
- Backup rotation: 4-hour overlap windows (08:00-12:00 / 12:00-16:00 shift handoffs)
- Cross-team liaison: Elena Park (observability/product) — handles dashboard anomalies & customer comms

Regional coverage cheatsheet (quick knobs):
- us-west-2: throttle 0.7 -> 0.5 if p95 increases >200ms vs baseline for 3 consecutive samples (5m windows)
- eu-west-1: autorollback threshold: error rate >1.5% sustained for 10m or latency tail 2x baseline
- ap-southeast-1: use model-variant v2-lite fallback at 30% if KV cache miss ratio >12%
- global fallback policy: if any two primary regions hit thresholds, flip to read-only fallback (non-blocking) + enable enhanced sampling

Telemetry watchlist (quick checks):
- p95 latency (per region and per-customer tier)
- token-generation timeouts / repeated cancel events
- upstream GPU saturation (% util) and OOM logs
- KV cache hit ratio (prefix hit) by model variant
- Error budget burn (per route) — >30% in 1h requires go/no-go review
- Drift signal: increase in short negative feedbacks from canary prompts (>10% day-over-day)

Smoke tests (preflight and rolling):
- Preflight (T-1h): basic gen smoke x10 prompts (sanity & safety) — pass = 0 failures, no regressions on quality metric set
- Canary quick-checks (phase A): 50 synthetic requests injected across 5 shards, assert latency/p95 within 1.25x baseline and zero critical errors
- Regional post-roll checks (every 2h): embedding sanity on production schema, token distribution metrics, customer-critical route passes

Rollback / mitigation ladder (fastest paths):
1) Immediate throttle to 10% acceptance (safest short-term stop)
2) Route to variant-lite model (v2-lite) while preserving client-compatibility headers
3) Full rollback: revert model switch + restore previous routing policy (requires release steward signoff)
4) Hotfix: apply patch to inference config (if small change) and soft-redeploy (only with tests green)

Communications (who says what):
- Internal ops channels: #release-orchestra (primary), #sre-oncall (escalation)
- Customer comms: Elena Park drafts standby message templates (if SLO breach >1h affecting >5% customers)
- Exec alert: page on-call PM and standby exec if >2 region failures or major regressions

Preflight checklist (T-24h -> T-15m):
- T-24h: finalize rollout JSON config, upload to config-store, sanity-check overlap rules (Jordan)
- T-12h: confirm capacity targets and warm pools for Dedicated tenants (Asha + infra)
- T-6h: validate traffic shaping scripts in staging (Miguel)
- T-2h: telemetry dashboards copied + baseline snapshots stored (Elena)
- T-30m: canary script loaded, smoke harness connected, alerts verified (all)
- T-5m: channel check-in, escalation ladder pinned to top of thread

Hourly calendar (sketch for Phase C ramp):
- 12:00 UTC: shift handoff + current metrics snapshot (owner on duty)
- 13:00 UTC: hold point — review p95 and errors, decide +10% or hold
- 14:00 UTC: if stable, ramp another +20% and re-run regional quick-smoke
- 16:00 UTC: converge logs to postmortem buffer if anomalies present; assign action owners
- 20:00 UTC: nightshift overlap — ensure backup steward in channel

Known open questions / risks (notes to self):
- KV cache miss threshold needs re-evaluation vs real-user traffic (our staging misses underrepresent production micro-burst patterns). Can we add a synthetic heating job? (action: Miguel)
- Customer route X uses nonstandard timeout; confirm fallback-compatible behavior before full ramp (action: Elena)
- Regional infra maintenance in eu-west-1 scheduled same day (TBD) — check blackout windows with infra calendar

Quick templates (copy-paste):
- Canary pass blurb: "Canary completed for region <region> at <time> — p95 within expected bounds; promoting to next cohort per schedule."
- Canary fail blurb: "Canary failed for <region> — elevated p95 (x) and error rate (y). Initiated throttle -> fallback and paused ramp. Triage assigned: <owner>."

Post-release notes stub (for later expansion):
- Summary: feature X released with progressive regional ramp; final completion 2028-06-16 11:12 UTC.
- Observed anomalies: transient p99 spike in us-west-2 at T+3h due to KV GC timing; mitigated by variant fallback.
- Action items: add KV heating job, update regional throttle defaults, postmortem scheduled 2028-06-18 10:00 UTC.

Appendix (links):
- Full runbook: CONFLUENCE-12345
- Release config: github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-configs/releases/2028-06-x
- Telemetry dashboards: dash://telemetry/release/2028-06-x

Endnotes:
This doc is intentionally compact — meant for pocket reference and shift use. Keep the full runbook version authoritative. If you copy this out to shift rotas, add the live links and put the steward on the first line.

-- Jordan R. (release steward)
summary: Compact operational pocket for a 72-hour staged rollout emphasizing regional thresholds, staffing, telemetry checks and rapid mitigation steps. Use alongside the full runbook.
